sentences.text: Icadyptes was an extinct genus of giant penguins that lived in the Late Eocene tropics of South America.
This animal possessed an exceptionally long, spear-like beak that resembled that of a heron.
The estimated standing height of this species is 1.5 meters.
Icadyptes salasi is classified in the family Spheniscidae and the subfamily Palaeeudyptinae.
It is an extinct species of sphenisciform bird belonging to the family Spheniscidae.
The genus name combines 'Ica', the region where the fossil was found, and 'dyptes', the Greek word for diver.
A well-preserved skeleton was discovered on the southern coast of Peru alongside the early Eocene species Perudyptes devriesi.
The fossils were discovered by the team of North Carolina State University paleontologist Dr. Julia Clarke.
Fossils of Icadyptes salasi and Perudyptes devriesi were discovered in 2005 by a team of Peruvian paleontologists.
Icadyptes salasi stood about 150 cm tall and was found in the desert coasts of the Ica region in southern Peru.
The species name 'salasi' honors the noted Peruvian paleontologist Rodolfo Salas.
Researchers believe the long, pointed beak of Icadyptes may represent the ancestral shape for all penguins.
Today, only a few penguin species, such as the African and Galapagos penguins, prefer the warm climates that Icadyptes inhabited.
Because Icadyptes salasi lived in warm Peru, penguins must have adapted to warm climates approximately 30 million years earlier than previously thought.
The fossil range of Icadyptes spans the Late Eocene, specifically the Divisaderan to Tinguirirican stages.
Icadyptes lived between 37.71 and 33.9 million years ago during the Priabonian stage.
It is debated whether penguins evolved near the poles and migrated to the equator only 10 million years ago, as the discovery of Icadyptes suggests an earlier adaptation to warm climates.
